title: DShuffle: DPU-Optimized Shuffle Framework for Large-scale Data Processing
problem: Shuffle operations in large-scale distributed data processing are CPU-bound and create network bottlenecks that limit throughput and waste computational resources. Traditional CPU-based shuffle implementations cannot efficiently handle the data reorganization demands of modern scale-out systems.
motivation: Offloading shuffle to specialized DPU hardware can eliminate CPU bottlenecks, reduce network congestion, and improve energy efficiency of distributed data processing pipelines.
method: DShuffle deploys shuffle logic to Data Processing Units (DPUs) located at the network boundary, leveraging their proximity to network interfaces and local memory hierarchy. The framework optimizes packet routing and data reorganization patterns to minimize network traffic and CPU-DPU communication overhead. It integrates with existing distributed processing frameworks through a transparent shuffle abstraction layer.
key_novelty: Hardware acceleration of shuffle operations by moving data reorganization from CPU to specialized DPUs at the network edge, eliminating shuffle as a system bottleneck.
contributions: DPU-based shuffle framework architecture and implementation
Optimized algorithms for network-efficient data reorganization on DPU hardware
Integration mechanism for compatibility with existing distributed data processing systems
Performance characterization showing significant improvements over CPU-based shuffles
